issues.problem: The role claims U_KENJI is 'not a member of core-infra,' but base_seed.channel_members explicitly contains {"channel_id":"C_INFRA","user_id":"U_KENJI"}. The role's own text is even self-contradictory ('member of product-growth and core-infra channels but not core-infra'). Since U_KENJI actually holds a core-infra membership record, adding an eyes reaction by U_KENJI on the product-growth message (as planned in negative_growth_reaction) would make product-growth satisfy the exact same condition as the intended positive channels (engineering, model-research), turning it into an accidental third match rather than a negative.
issues.repair: Either pick a different reactor for the product-growth negative who genuinely lacks any C_INFRA membership row (e.g., U_INCOGNITO, who per the seed is only in C_GROWTH), or remove U_KENJI's C_INFRA membership from the seed if the writer intends to keep U_KENJI as the negative reactor.

rationale: The design's core semantic contract is: a channel qualifies iff one of its messages has an eyes reaction from a user who also has a conversation-membership record in core-infra. The negative_growth_channel/reaction/reactor triple is supposed to demonstrate a channel that fails only because the reactor lacks core-infra membership. But the supplied base_seed already contains a channel_members row proving U_KENJI IS a core-infra member, directly contradicting the role's stated reasoning and the exposure_qualification's 'negative' designation. If compiled as specified, product-growth would incorrectly qualify as a match, breaking the intended 2-match/2-negative structure the obligation's target_roles rely on (only engineering and model-research are listed as targets). This is a factual/referential defect in the design against its own base seed, not merely a stylistic issue, so it cannot pass validity as written.
